title: Personal Checking: Stop Payment Orders on Paper Checks and Their Renewal
content:
## What an order covers

A Personal Checking stop payment order applies to one paper check, pinned down by its serial number together with the precise amount the customer states; the payee is noted as the customer names it. Orders exist only on tiers that allow paper checks. This rule has nothing to say about stopping an ACH debit or an official check.

## When an order can be placed

- The check must still be unpaid. A check counts as paid once the account shows a paid-check debit bearing the same check number; this is read from the account's own entries.
- If the check already carries an order that has not lapsed, no second order is placed; the existing order is renewed.

## Life of an order

An order lapses at the end of 6 calendar months counted from its order date. Its lapse date is the order date moved forward by 6 calendar months; where that month has no such day, the last day of that month is used.

## Renewal

- An order that has not lapsed may be renewed on any date up to and including its lapse date. The six-month reckoning starts from the date the renewed order itself was placed.
- A renewal is recorded as a new order that names the order it renews. Its own lapse date is the renewal's order date moved forward by 6 calendar months, with the same month-end fallback.
- A lapsed order cannot be renewed. If the check is still unpaid, a fresh order is placed.

## Date cases (hypothetical)

| Order date | Lapse date | Renewal on | Allowed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 March 2026 | 15 September 2026 | 15 September 2026 | yes |
| 15 March 2026 | 15 September 2026 | 16 September 2026 | no — a new order instead, if the check is unpaid |
| 31 August 2026 | 28 February 2027 | 1 February 2027 | yes; the renewal lapses 1 August 2027 |

## Points of judgement

- A customer asking to stop check 1043 when the account already shows check 1043 paid cannot have a stop placed.
- On a checkless tier no stop order can be placed or renewed.
